result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by an elevated rail structure that creates significant shadowing and visual obstructions. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the lack of marked crossings and the presence of large support pillars on the walkway reduce the overall safety and comfort for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Infrastructure
hazards.description: Large concrete pillars supporting the elevated rail structure create significant blind spots for both pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway along the sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Controlled Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals, forcing pedestrians to cross at unmarked locations.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire visible stretch of the roadway

hazards.name: Poor Lighting/Shadowing
hazards.description: The elevated structure creates deep shadows during the day, which may reduce the visibility of pedestrians to motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Underneath the blue steel rail structure

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks with appropriate signage to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting fixtures underneath the elevated structure to improve visibility and the sense of security for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility around the pillars.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, well-maintained sidewalk beneath an elevated structure, providing a clear path for walking. However, the lack of a physical buffer from the roadway and the absence of marked crossings in this mid-block section reduce overall safety and comfort.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lane without any physical separation like trees, bollards, or a furniture zone.

hazards.name: Absence of mid-block crossing
hazards.description: There are no marked pedestrian crossings visible in this stretch, which may lead to unsafe crossing behavior.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or furniture zone to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and moving vehicles.

interventions.title: Mid-block Pedestrian Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility crosswalk with curb extensions to improve pedestrian safety and connectivity across the roadway.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a large elevated rail structure, which creates a shadowed and somewhat industrial atmosphere. While continuous sidewalks are present on both sides, the large support pillars on the left and parked cars on the right create visual and physical obstructions.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Infrastructure
hazards.description: Large concrete pillars supporting the elevated rail structure create significant blind spots for both pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway, along the sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals visible, forcing pedestrians to cross at unmarked locations if needed.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing with High-Visibility Markings
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with high-visibility paint and pedestrian-activated warning lights to provide a safe crossing point.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Enhanced Under-Structure Lighting
interventions.description: Improve lighting specifically under the elevated rail structure to eliminate dark spots and increase personal security.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a continuous sidewalk along a mixed-use block, but it lacks a buffer from the roadway. A utility pole is positioned in the center of the walkway, creating an obstruction, and a roll-down door indicates a vehicle access point across the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large utility pole is located in the middle of the sidewalk, significantly narrowing the clear walking path and creating an accessibility barrier.

hazards.name: Vehicle Conflict Point
hazards.description: A roll-down door for a car wash indicates a location where vehicles cross the pedestrian walkway.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer
interventions.description: Install a planting strip or furniture zone to separate pedestrians from moving traffic and provide space for utility poles.

interventions.title: Clear Path Maintenance
interventions.description: Relocate the utility pole or widen the sidewalk to ensure a minimum 5-foot clear walking path is maintained.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve pedestrian visibility.
